description: A challenging 7-mile sub-alpine loop through the San Francisco Peaks, featuring otherworldly avalanche scars and grizzly forests.
why_go: Experience otherworldly avalanche destruction and explore ancient grizzly forests.
Traverse some of the most unique terrain in the San Francisco Peaks.
See the massive avalanche damage from 2005 that reshaped the forest.

trail_segments.name: Abineau Trail
trail_segments.description: Steadily climbs through mixed conifers and tall aspens, with abundant moss in shaded areas.
trail_segments.features: Steep, loose soil; shaded mossy forest

trail_segments.name: Avalanche Scar
trail_segments.description: A striking 200-foot-wide, half-mile-long scar from the 2005 avalanche, still visibly impacting the forest.

recommendations: Hike counter-clockwise to avoid steep descents on loose soil.
Wear sturdy footwear suitable for challenging terrain.
Bring plenty of water and be prepared for elevation changes.
Prepare for shaded forest sections and open avalanche scar views.
season: Best visited in late spring through early fall
access: Trailhead located at Abineau Trailhead, accessible via Flagstaff roads
